title: MENINGOCOCCAL POLYSACCHARIDE VACCINES = VACCINS ANTIMÉNINGOCOCCIQUES POLYOSIDIQUES

sections.title: Page 1

summary.text: Opens a bilingual Weekly Epidemiological Record statement on meningococcal polysaccharide vaccines newly licensed in the United States against serogroups A and C. It reviews the history of meningococcal epidemics, the decline of serogroup C disease in military recruits after routine vaccination, and the current serogroup and age distribution of cases. The page ends with the issue's table of contents.

sections.extract: MENINGOCOCCAL POLYSACCHARIDE VACCINES U nited States of A merica. — Polysaccharide vaccines against diseases caused by Neisseria meningitidis serogroups A and C are now licensed in the United States. They are prepared as monovalent and as bivalent antigens. sections.title: Page 2

summary.text: Continues the meningococcal vaccine statement, describing the monovalent A, monovalent C and bivalent vaccines, evidence of effectiveness from Egypt and Brazil, and poor effectiveness of serogroup C vaccine under two years. It advises against routine civilian vaccination but recommends use in serogroup A or C outbreaks, for some travellers and as an adjunct for household contacts, noting mild side effects and caution in pregnancy. A French version and notes on polyvalent vaccine development follow.
